churn.plain: customers who bought before but no longer do

anomaly.plain: a value that is far from the usual

concentration.plain: depending too much on one thing

median.plain: the middle value when all values are sorted

standard_deviation.plain: how spread out the values are

margin.plain: the share of sales that remains as profit

win_rate.plain: the share of deals that were won

average.plain: the sum of values divided by their number

mode.plain: the value that appears most often

variance.plain: how far values are from their average, squared

range.plain: the gap between the smallest and the largest value

quartile.plain: one of three points that split sorted values into four equal parts

percentile.plain: the value below which a given share of the data falls

iqr.plain: the spread of the middle half of the values

outlier.plain: a value far away from most others

skewness.plain: when most values are small but a few are very large

distribution.plain: how values are spread across their range

histogram.plain: a chart that counts how many values fall in each range

boxplot.plain: a chart that shows the middle half, the middle and the extremes

p_value.plain: how likely a result is to be pure chance

significance.plain: a result unlikely to be chance

confidence_interval.plain: the range where the true value most likely lies

confidence_level.plain: how sure we are about a finding

sample.plain: the part of the data that was examined

z_score.plain: how many typical steps a value is from the average

regression.plain: a line that shows how one measure changes with another

r_squared.plain: how much of the change a trend line explains

slope.plain: how much a value changes per step

trend.plain: the general direction a value moves over time

seasonality.plain: a pattern that repeats every year, month or week

moving_average.plain: the average of the latest few periods

anova.plain: a test of whether several groups differ

t_test.plain: a test of whether two groups differ

chi_square.plain: a test of whether two categories are linked

effect_size.plain: how big a difference is, not only whether it exists

spearman.plain: a link measure that only looks at ranks

pearson.plain: a link measure for straight-line relationships

causation.plain: when one thing really makes another happen

null_value.plain: an empty cell with no data

duplicate.plain: a record that appears more than once

cardinality.plain: how many different values a column has

cohort.plain: a group of customers who started in the same period

segment.plain: a group of similar customers, products or records

benchmark.plain: a standard value used for comparison

baseline.plain: the usual level before a change

threshold.plain: a limit that triggers attention when crossed

growth_rate.plain: how fast a value grows, as a percentage

cagr.plain: the average yearly growth over several years

yoy.plain: a comparison with the same period last year

mom.plain: a comparison with the previous month

ytd.plain: from the start of this year until today

ratio.plain: how many times one number is larger than another

share.plain: a part of the whole, in percent

pareto.plain: a few causes usually bring most of the result

hhi.plain: a number that shows how unevenly something is shared

gini.plain: a number for how unequal a distribution is

weighted_average.plain: an average where bigger items count more

top_n.plain: the first few items when sorted from largest

profit.plain: money left after paying all costs

gross_profit.plain: sales minus the direct cost of goods

net_profit.plain: what remains after every cost and tax

gross_margin.plain: the share of sales left after the cost of goods

operating_margin.plain: the share of sales left after running costs

cost_of_goods.plain: what it cost to buy or make the goods sold

expense.plain: money spent to run the business

fixed_cost.plain: a cost that stays the same whatever you sell

variable_cost.plain: a cost that grows with sales

overhead.plain: regular costs not tied to one product

ebitda.plain: profit before interest, tax and wear-and-tear

cash_flow.plain: money coming in minus money going out

liquidity.plain: how quickly you can turn assets into cash

balance_sheet.plain: a list of what a business owns and owes

asset.plain: something of value that a business owns

equity.plain: what is left for owners after paying all debts

depreciation.plain: the yearly loss in value of equipment

budget.plain: a plan for how much to earn and spend

variance_to_plan.plain: the gap between actual and planned numbers

break_even.plain: the point where income equals costs

roi.plain: how much you earn compared with what you put in

payback.plain: the time it takes to earn back an investment

inflation.plain: the general rise of prices over time

exchange_rate.plain: the price of one currency in another

vat.plain: a tax added to the price of goods and services

discount.plain: a reduction of the normal price

markup.plain: the amount added to cost to get the price

npl.plain: a loan that is not being repaid on time

interest_rate.plain: the price of borrowing money, in percent

overdue.plain: not paid by the agreed date

deposit.plain: money a customer keeps in a bank

loan.plain: money borrowed that must be paid back

pipeline.plain: all open deals and their expected value

funnel.plain: the steps a customer passes from first contact to purchase

conversion_rate.plain: the share that moves on to the next step

lead.plain: a person who may become a customer

qualified_lead.plain: a lead that is likely to buy

deal.plain: a possible sale being worked on

open_deal.plain: a deal that is not yet won or lost

stalled_deal.plain: a deal with no progress for a long time

sales_cycle.plain: the time from first contact to a closed deal

deal_size.plain: the average value of a won deal

quota.plain: the sales target set for a person or team

attainment.plain: how much of the target has been reached

forecast_sales.plain: the expected sales for a coming period

upsell.plain: selling a more expensive version to an existing customer

cross_sell.plain: selling an extra product to an existing customer

retention.plain: the share of customers who stay

loyalty.plain: how willing customers are to buy again

repeat_purchase.plain: a purchase by a customer who bought before

ltv.plain: all money a customer is expected to bring

cac.plain: what it costs to win one new customer

arpu.plain: the average income from one customer

average_check.plain: the average amount of one purchase

basket.plain: how many items are in one purchase

sku.plain: a unique code for each product variant

turnover.plain: how often stock is sold and replaced

stockout.plain: when a product is sold out

refund.plain: money given back to a customer

channel.plain: the way customers buy, such as shop or online

territory.plain: the area or customers one seller is responsible for

owner.plain: the person responsible for a deal or customer

source.plain: where a customer or deal came from

promotion.plain: a short offer to boost sales

campaign.plain: a planned set of marketing actions

ctr.plain: the share of people who click after seeing

roas.plain: how much sales each advertising sum brings

nps.plain: a score showing how likely customers are to recommend you

sla.plain: a promise about how fast you will respond

backlog.plain: work or orders waiting to be handled

throughput.plain: how much work is finished in a period

utilization.plain: the share of available capacity that is used

tenure.plain: how long a person has worked here

dataset.plain: a table or set of tables with your data

column.plain: one field of a table, such as date or amount

schema.plain: the list of columns and their types

metric.plain: a number that measures something, such as revenue

dimension.plain: a way to split numbers, such as by region

filter.plain: a rule that keeps only some of the data

drill_down.plain: looking at the details behind a number

cross_filter.plain: clicking one chart to filter all the others

dashboard.plain: a page with the key numbers and charts

kpi_tile.plain: a small tile showing one key number

gauge.plain: a dial chart that shows progress toward a target

treemap.plain: a chart of nested rectangles sized by value

heatmap.plain: a grid where color shows the size of a value

waterfall.plain: a chart that shows how steps add up to a total

scatter.plain: a chart of dots comparing two measures

stacked_chart.plain: a chart where parts are piled up to a total

donut.plain: a ring chart that shows shares of a whole

legend.plain: the key that explains colors in a chart

axis.plain: the line with numbers or labels along a chart

tooltip.plain: a small note that appears when you point at something

grain.plain: how detailed the data is, such as daily or monthly

aggregation.plain: combining many rows into one number

join.plain: linking two tables through a common column

primary_key.plain: a value that identifies one row only

data_quality.plain: how complete and correct your data is

data_cleaning.plain: fixing mistakes and gaps in data

pii.plain: information that identifies a person, such as a phone number

masking.plain: hiding part of a value to protect privacy

privacy_mode.plain: the setting that decides what leaves your computer

audit_log.plain: a record of who did what and when

verified_answer.plain: an answer that passed our automatic check

unverified_answer.plain: an answer that did not pass the check

sql.plain: the language used to ask a database a question

export.plain: saving a result as a file

retention_policy.plain: how long data is kept before deletion

template.plain: a ready layout you can start from

domain.plain: the kind of data, such as retail or banking

period.plain: a stretch of time such as a week or a month

fiscal_year.plain: the twelve months a company uses for accounts
